metadata.title: Unautomated Security
metadata.purpose: Provenance Gatekeeper development log, Week 7 — replacing manual verification with a pytest harness and a GitHub Actions pipeline that rebuilds the stack, fires the adversarial suite at it, and blocks the merge when anything slips through.

metadata.audience: Humanitarians AI fellows and practitioners following the Provenance Gatekeeper build
metadata.source: Week 7: CI/CD Pipeline & Automated Testing — Video Script, Provenance Gatekeeper Development Log. Supplied 2026-10-17.
metadata.dual_render: 16:9 master + 9:16 companion, both required. Every pattern has a registered <Pattern>916 variant. ZERO new components. Built straight to ./art final — no review cut — so no beat chip or timecode is ever drawn and GATE V runs on both aspects.
metadata.color_semantics: Claude FIDELITY skin — cream #FAF9F5 / stage #F2F0E9, warm ink #3D3929, terracotta #D97757 as the ONE accent. The script's green PASS / red X pair maps to unfilled ink for passing and terracotta for failing: a green would be a second accent and is the contrast colour-blind viewers lose.
metadata.channel_note: Narrated in the FIRST PERSON by Onkar Bhujbal, matching the script's own Scene 1 VO. The Kokoro am_onyx voice is a synthetic read of Onkar's own script, not a clone of his voice.

The reel is TITLED 'Unautomated Security' (from the script's own closing line) because the Week 1 reel in this same series is already titled 'Works On My Machine' and two near-identical titles would collide in the playlist.

beats.narration_text: Hi, I am Onkar Bhujbal. Last week we built a regex parser for the Provenance Gatekeeper that extracts financial data from unpredictable A.I. text. It worked perfectly on my local machine. But enterprise software is not about what works locally — it is about what survives in production. This week we strip away manual testing and build an automated continuous integration pipeline.

beats.honesty_note: The 4-of-19 / 15-case split is ILLUSTRATIVE — it dramatises the manual-testing gap the script describes. No real suite size or failure count was supplied, and none is claimed as measured.

beats.narration_text: Week seven added no new detection logic at all. It added the thing that makes last week's logic trustworthy next month — a suite that runs itself, on a machine that is not mine, every single time anyone touches the code.

beats.narration_text: We started by writing strict unit tests with pytest. We codified every adversarial scenario we knew of — valid strings, magnitude errors, S.Q.L. injections — into a test underscore main dot py file. Instead of running scripts by hand and eyeballing the output, we now have a programmatic harness that proves the normalization layer behaves exactly as intended.
beats.new_visual_element: Two stages — write the cases, then let the harness run them

beats.narration_text: But developers forget to run tests. To remove the human, we integrated GitHub Actions. We configured a workflow with path filtering, so every time new code is pushed to the Gatekeeper directory, GitHub spins up a pristine Ubuntu runner, installs our dependencies, and boots the FastAPI and ChromaDB architecture inside Docker.

beats.narration_text: So let's push a pull request that lets one hallucinated payload through, and watch whether the pipeline lets it reach the main branch.
beats.new_visual_element: Ask micro-beat — the prompt that fires the pipeline at a bad PR

show.event: composer already framed; the prompt types in
running indicator reads 'bombarding the API…'; no output lines — the next beat IS the output

props.command: Open a PR where one adversarial payload slips past the evaluation logic, run the full stress test in Actions, and show me the merge state.

beats.authoring_note: ASK → RESULT pair: BASK is the ask, B04 is the result (ASK→RESULT LAW).

beats.narration_text: Once the environment is live, the pipeline bombards our own A.P.I. with the adversarial stress test. If a single hallucinated payload slips through the logic, the build fails and the code is blocked from merging. We have effectively built a perimeter that regressions cannot physically cross into the main branch.
beats.new_visual_element: The failing test, beside the merge that never arms

show.event: left panel lands: the pytest output, one assertion failing
right panel lands: PULL REQUEST #62 · GitHub Actions
check counter climbs, then STOPS short of the total
the button stays MERGE BLOCKED — the regression cannot enter main
blocked state holds through the cut

props.code:
test_magnitude_error ......... PASS
test_sql_injection ........... PASS
test_null_payload ............ PASS
test_directional_error ....... FAIL

  assert verdict == "FAIL"
  E  AssertionError: got "PASS"

1 failed, 3 passed

beats.honesty_note: PR #62, the 18-of-19 counts and the four named tests are ILLUSTRATIVE — no real test_main.py, suite size or Actions run was supplied. The failing case is a directional error, which is the exact blind spot the Week 2 reel identified, so the example is consistent with the series rather than arbitrary. The counter stops one short so the merge button never arms, which is the beat's claim.

beats.narration_text: So stop testing your A.I. logic by hand. Write unit tests for your extraction layer and force your repository to run them on every commit. Unautomated security is just a suggestion.
beats.new_visual_element: The command, and the setting that gives it teeth

show.event: code card opens on a hard cut; traffic-light dot arms terracotta
the pytest command reveals
the TASK line lands
the branch-protection note lands last — the part that makes red mean blocked

props.title: run_tests.sh
props.code:
python -m pytest tests/test_main.py -v

# TASK: run this on every commit, not
# when you remember to.

# Then mark the Actions check REQUIRED
# in branch protection.
#
# A failing check nobody must obey is
# a suggestion. Required makes it a wall.

beats.authoring_note: The branch-protection note is the reel's addition. The script's Scene 4 says the pipeline 'blocks' the merge — true only when the check is marked required; otherwise Actions reports red and the merge button still works.

beats.narration_text: And once the pipeline is green, here is the prompt worth running. Give a model your test file and your parser, and ask which adversarial categories you have no test for at all. A suite that only contains the attacks you already thought of will pass forever, right up until it matters.
beats.new_visual_element: Handoff — the viewer's prompt, read aloud

props.command: Here is my test_main.py and my parser. Group my cases by attack category, name the categories I have NO test for, and write one failing test for each gap.

beats.narration_text: A test you have to remember to run is not a test. Unautomated security is just a suggestion. Onkar Bhujbal, for Humanitarians AI.
